bead.title: Fix set_high_water and append-sequence TOCTOU for multi-node Postgres
bead.description:
PROBLEM
Under a connection pool, two callers can both pass the high-water monotonic check and regress it; the append MAX(seq)+1 read-then-insert has the same race. The system must work multi-node (operator requirement, 2026-07-03), and ADR-013 (log as single source of truth) makes the log append the sole serialization point — this race is its hard prerequisite.

CURRENT STATE
- crates/pqueue-postgres/src/lib.rs:16-46 documents the TOCTOU as known future work.
- set_high_water: SELECT (:1552) -> precedes check (:1559) -> INSERT/UPSERT (:1564), non-atomic across connections.
- Append allocates MAX(seq)+1 (:232) then inserts (:241).
- Both are serialized today only by a process Mutex — cross-process/multi-node unsafe.

PROPOSED FIX
Fold the monotonic guard into a single conditional statement (UPDATE ... WHERE (epoch,seq) < (new), or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE), and make append sequence allocation atomic (conditional insert with returning, per-queue counter row under FOR UPDATE, or a DB sequence). Remove reliance on the process Mutex for cross-connection safety.

NON-SCOPE
- Connection pool introduction and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim path (separate scale-out work).
- sqlite backends (whole-db lock already serializes).
bead.acceptance:
1. postgres_high_water_concurrent_monotonic: two concurrent connections race set_high_water from the same prior value; the stored value never regresses. cargo test -p pqueue-postgres postgres_high_water_concurrent_monotonic
2. postgres_append_concurrent_sequence_no_gap_no_dup: two concurrent appends yield contiguous, unique sequences or a clean rollback. cargo test -p pqueue-postgres postgres_append_concurrent_sequence_no_gap_no_dup
3. cargo test -p pqueue-postgres passes.
